summary: When the hero ends Fumbling over a petrifying floor corpse without foot armor or Stone_resistance, timeout.c:slip_or_trip sets the killer name and calls trap.c:instapetrify. JavaScript already detects the same condition and sets the same killer name, but replaces the void call with note_unported('trap.c instapetrify'). The omitted helper emits the urgent stoning message and enters the normal hero-death path, so the recorded trip at step 341 is followed by petrification in C at step 342 while JavaScript continues the turn.

source.branch: When an object is under the hero on foot, uarmf is absent, the object is a corpse whose species touch-petrifies, and Stone_resistance is false, C writes the tripping-over killer cause and calls the void trap.c:instapetrify helper.
callers: timeout.c:nh_timeout calls slip_or_trip after the Fumbling timeout reaches zero; the case expires Fumbling while the hero stands over the corpse.
js/timeout.js:nh_timeout reaches slip_or_trip after property expiry. Its matching corpse branch currently records trap.c instapetrify as unported rather than calling the existing js/trap.js helper.
dependencies: trap.c:instapetrify is already implemented and exported as async instapetrify() from js/trap.js. C discards its void return; JavaScript must await the helper so its urgent stoning message and done(STONING) effects complete before the turn continues.
js/trap.js imports timeout.js helpers, so use a function-local dynamic import from timeout.js to avoid adding a static cycle.

evidence: The v56 manifest identifies timeout.c:slip_or_trip lines 1253-1259 and describes the missing existing trap.js instapetrify caller for an ungloved hero who trips over a petrifying corpse.

Read upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/timeout.c:slip_or_trip (1222-1341), especially lines 1256-1260: C checks !uarmf, CORPSE, touch_petrifies, and !Stone_resistance; it sets svk.killer.name to 'tripping over ... corpse' and calls instapetrify(svk.killer.name). Read trap.c:instapetrify (3844-3855): it emits the urgent 'You turn to stone...' message, sets KILLED_BY, preserves the killer cause, and calls done(STONING).

The baseline scan at a7c565dc80155e5c934fbb92aaab3474b12f63ba reproduces the v56 divergence at segment 0 step 342. C and JS match through step 341; at step 342 C shows the urgent petrification message while JS continues with an unrelated turn message and later draws rn2(5). The scan's unported set contains trap.c instapetrify.

js/timeout.js:slip_or_trip already computes the same source predicate and killer cause at lines 822-830, then calls note_unported('trap.c instapetrify'). The helper exists at js/trap.js:instapetrify. The bounded correction is to call and await the existing helper through a function-local dynamic import, preserving the existing planning guard and the C void-result behavior.
